Definition: to vacillate, i.e. reel or stray (literally or figuratively); also causative of both
BiblicalUsage: Isaiah says all we like sheep have gone astray, every one to his own way. Joseph's brothers find him wandering in the field at Shechem; Jeremiah says God's people have been lost sheep, led astray by their shepherds; Proverbs says those who devise evil err, and Ezekiel charges the Levites who went astray after idols. The word is wandering with a moral edge: straying from the path, from the shepherd, and from God.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that going astray is the Bible's plainest picture of sin. I believe Isaiah 53:6 says it best — we have all done it, every one to his own way — and that is exactly why the Lord laid on Him the iniquity of us all.
